alert.port_scan.title: Port scan: {src} → {dst} ({n_ports} ports)
alert.port_scan.explanation: Host {src} attempted connections to {n_ports} distinct ports on {dst} within {duration}s with no responses — consistent with a SYN port scan.
alert.beaconing.title: Beaconing: {src} → {dst}:{dport} every {mean}s
alert.beaconing.explanation: Host {src} connected to {dst}:{dport} {conn_count} times with machine-precise ~{mean}s intervals (jitter {std}s). Periodic beacons like this are a hallmark of C2 check-ins or scheduled implants.
alert.dns_tunneling.title: DNS tunneling indicators from {client}
alert.dns_tunneling.explanation: Host {client} sent {queries} DNS queries with encoded-looking labels (longest {max_label} chars) across {unique_sub} unique subdomains — a pattern consistent with DNS tunneling (data exfiltration over DNS).
alert.nxdomain_burst.title: Excessive NXDOMAIN from {client} ({nx} failed lookups)
alert.nxdomain_burst.explanation: Host {client} generated {nx} NXDOMAIN responses ({rate}% of its DNS traffic). Bursts of failed lookups can indicate DGA malware, typo-squat probing, or DNS reconnaissance.
alert.suspicious_port.title: Suspicious port: {src} → {dst}:{port}
alert.suspicious_port.explanation: Host {src} communicated with {dst} on port {port}, commonly associated with {association}.
alert.excessive_connection_failures.expl: Host {src} attempted {failed} connections to {dst} on ports {ports} without any completing — service outage, blocked firewall rule, or dead destination.
alert.connection_without_dns.title: Direct IP connection: {src} → {dst}:{dport} (no DNS)
alert.connection_without_dns.explanation: Host {src} connected to {dst}:{dport} without any DNS lookup resolving it in this capture. Hardcoded destinations are common in malware config.
alert.connection_without_dns.reason.no_d: {dst} was never resolved by any DNS query
alert.high_outbound_volume.title: High outbound volume from {host} ({bytes} bytes)
alert.high_outbound_volume.explanation: Host {host} accounts for {share}% of outbound traffic ({bytes} bytes) — possible data exfiltration or backup activity.
alert.arp_spoofing.title: ARP conflict: {ip} claimed by {mac_count} MACs
alert.arp_spoofing.explanation: IP address {ip} was claimed by {mac_count} different MAC addresses in ARP traffic — classic ARP-spoofing / man-in-the-middle signature (attacker poisons the gateway mapping).
alert.lateral_movement.title: Lateral movement: {src} → {target_count} internal hosts (admin ports)
alert.lateral_movement.explanation: Internal host {src} connected to {target_count} other internal hosts on administrative ports {admin_ports}. This internal fan-out pattern is characteristic of post-compromise lateral movement.
alert.dga_domain.title: DGA-like domains from {client} ({count} algorithmic names)
alert.dga_domain.explanation: Host {client} looked up {count} high-entropy, dictionary-less domains (capture baseline entropy {baseline}). Domains like these are usually generated by malware DGAs to evade static blocklists.
alert.dga_domain.reason.high_entropy.det: {count} domains with entropy well above baseline ({baseline})
alert.dga_domain.reason.dict_less.detail: long consonant runs, no readable words
alert.dga_domain.reason.many_nxdomain.de: {nx} domains failed to resolve (typical of DGA rotation)
alert.data_exfiltration.title: Possible exfiltration: {src} → {dst} ({bytes} bytes)
alert.data_exfiltration.explanation_firs: Host {src} transferred {bytes} bytes to external host {dst} (which was never resolved via DNS — first contact) — consistent with data exfiltration.
alert.data_exfiltration.explanation_shor: Host {src} transferred {bytes} bytes to external host {dst} (in a short window) — consistent with data exfiltration.
alert.data_exfiltration.reason.first_con: {dst} never resolved via DNS in this capture
alert.low_slow_beaconing.title: Low-and-slow beacon: {src} → {dst}:{dport} every {minutes}min
alert.low_slow_beaconing.explanation: Host {src} checked in with {dst}:{dport} {conn_count} times at regular ~{minutes}-minute intervals — low-and-slow C2 cadence that evades short-window rate-based detection.
alert.low_slow_beaconing.reason.low_slow: few, spread-out check-ins designed to evade rate alerts
alert.suspicious_user_agent.title: Suspicious user agent: {label} ({count} requests)
alert.suspicious_user_agent.explanation: {count} HTTP requests carried a user agent matching {label} — "{ua}". Legitimate browsers rarely send these fingerprints.
